column1: # *** THE VARIANT SWEEP TURNED ON THE CENTRAL QUESTION, 15 September 2026. ***
# Spelling the surname three ways found eight documents for SANCHO that this archive had missed.
# The same method was then pointed at PABLO ARMANDO and at JUAN CARLOS, which is what the whole
# archive exists to answer. *** It did not find them - and this time the null is controlled. ***
*** PABLO ARMANDO IS ABSENT FROM FAMILYSEARCH FULL TEXT UNDER EVERY SPELLING TRIED ***
column2: *** "Pablo Armando Lerena" - No Results Found. "Pablo Armando Llerena" - No Results Found. "Pablo Armando Lorena" - No Results Found. *** All three returned zero WITH the 'No Results Found' message present, not a bare zero. *** CONTROL, run in the same form and the same session, immediately before: "Juan Carlos Lerena" - TWO DOCUMENTS. ***
column4: *** This is the first time the full-text corpus has been tested for him BY NAME rather than by reading registers page by page. *** Everything this archive knows about his absence from Rosario came from reading the baptism index end to end for 1731-1901 and the register act by act for February and March 1882. *** This is an independent negative by a different method, over a corpus that includes documents no index covers. *** *** IT DOES NOT MEAN HE WAS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN. *** Full text covers a fraction of what is filmed, the machine mangles this surname into at least seven forms, and a baptism act names a child by forename alone in the sentence that matters. *** What it does mean is that no transcribed document anywhere in that corpus puts PABLO ARMANDO next to any spelling of this surname. ***

column1: *** AND THE TWO 'JUAN CARLOS' HITS ARE BOTH NAMESAKES, CHECKED AND EXCLUDED ***
column2: *** (1) "Don JUAN CARLOS GONZALEZ LERENA" *** - Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1856-1932, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-NNW8, 8 November 192-: dispensed the three conciliar proclamas for a marriage to Concepcion Petrona Urbano. *** LERENA is his SECOND surname, his mother's - the same shape as the 'del Campo Lerena Juan Carlos' that is the only Juan Carlos Lerena in all of Geneanet. *** *** (2) "Juan Carlos", baptised at San Nicolas de Bari, Retiro, Buenos Aires, 30 August 1910 *** - ark 3:1:939D-GD9T-LM - "que nacio el dia diez de Julio del ano mil novecientos diez, hijo legitimo de D. RAFAEL LLERENA natural del Pais de veinte y nueve anos de edad, y de Dona MARIA CARLOTA AMADEO LASTRA", of Calle Cerrito 535.
column3: PRIMARY for both - transcripts read here
column4: *** NEITHER CAN BE PABLO ARMANDO'S FATHER. *** The enrolment card's Juan Carlos Lerena carries LERENA as the paternal surname and must have been born by about the 1850s to father a son in 1882. *** One of these has Lerena from his mother and marries in the 1920s; the other was BORN in 1910. *** *** Recorded because both are the kind of hit a future reader will find and have to spend an hour excluding. *** *** The second is worth something else, though: it documents a LLERENA HOUSEHOLD IN BUENOS AIRES *** - Rafael Llerena, born about 1881, Argentine-born, living at Calle Cerrito 535 in 1910 with Maria Carlota Amadeo Lastra. This archive has been looking for Argentine Llerenas of that generation and did not have him.

column1: *** AND A FOURTH COSTUME FOR THE SAME TRAP, 15 September 2026 ***
column2: Three further searches were run late in the session - *** "Fidel Llerena", "Lerena y Maria Ruedas" and "Pablo Lorena" *** - and all three came back with *** zero results and no 'No Results Found' message. *** They looked exactly like the nulls recorded above. *** THE FAMILYSEARCH SESSION HAD SILENTLY EXPIRED and every request was being redirected to ident.familysearch.org, the sign-in page. ***
column3: *** NOT EVIDENCE. NOT RECORDED AS NULLS. ***
column4: *** The control caught it, and only the control. *** *** "Sancho Lerena" - a search that had returned three Canelones baptisms an hour earlier in the same session - was re-run and came back with zero links and a page title of "Sign-in to your account". *** *** A logged-out search engine returns the same shape as a genuine null: *** an empty result list. It does not say it has logged you out, and the page that arrives is not obviously an error. *** THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOW SEEN THE SAME TRAP FOUR TIMES IN A MONTH, in four different disguises: *** FamilySearch's results page rendering '(0)' while still loading; a Google Books API returning 'totalItems: None' on an HTTP 429 quota error; a blocked session returning Access Denied behind an empty body; and now an expired login redirecting to a sign-in form. *** The rule that has survived all four is the same one: a null is not written down until a control query in the same form returns a KNOWN result in the SAME session. *** *** Running the control is not a formality. It is the only thing that has ever caught this. ***
